mature_ideas.title: Relaxed Torque Formalism with Dynamical Inclination and Wind Braking for Isolated Pulsar Spin-Down
mature_ideas.hypothesis: The systematic deviations from n=3 in isolated pulsar spin-down can be explained by a unified torque model that incorporates time-varying magnetic inclination angle decay and relativistic wind braking, without requiring ad hoc magnetic field decay, provided the validity domain is restricted to pulsars with characteristic ages > 10^4 yr and surface fields < 10^13 G.
mature_ideas.central_hypothesis: The systematic deviations from n=3 in isolated pulsar spin-down can be explained by a unified torque model that incorporates time-varying magnetic inclination angle decay and relativistic wind braking, without requiring ad hoc magnetic field decay, provided the validity domain is restricted to pulsars with characteristic ages > 10^4 yr and surface fields < 10^13 G.
mature_ideas.scientific_object: isolated radio pulsars with measured braking indices
mature_ideas.mechanism: Torque function N(Omega) = -K Omega^3 [sin^2(alpha(t)) + eta(t)] where alpha(t) is the time-dependent magnetic inclination angle decaying as dot{alpha} < 0 and eta(t) is a wind-braking efficiency parameter; the effective braking index n_eff = Omega ddot{Omega}/dot{Omega}^2 deviates from 3 due to both sin^2(alpha) evolution and eta > 0 contributions.
mature_ideas.mechanism_or_relation: Torque function N(Omega) = -K Omega^3 [sin^2(alpha(t)) + eta(t)] where alpha(t) is the time-dependent magnetic inclination angle decaying as dot{alpha} < 0 and eta(t) is a wind-braking efficiency parameter; the effective braking index n_eff = Omega ddot{Omega}/dot{Omega}^2 deviates from 3 due to both sin^2(alpha) evolution and eta > 0 contributions.
assumptions: Magnetic field modulus B is approximately constant over spin-down timescales for non-magnetar pulsars
Inclination angle decay follows a secular trend driven by magnetospheric current evolution
Wind braking efficiency eta scales with spin-down luminosity and is negligible for old, slow pulsars
Validity restricted to isolated pulsars with negligible external torques from companions or fallback disks
evidence_basis: SURVEY_ANCHOR: negative dot alpha terms can account for observed spin-down anomalies
SURVEY_ANCHOR: Crab pulsar serves as a pivotal case study where combined dipole radiation and wind braking effects are quantified
PAPER_ANCHOR: W2590059791 demonstrates inclination angle decay modifies braking torque
mature_ideas.refinement_scope: Relax the vacuum dipole assumption by adding inclination decay and wind braking terms to the torque equation, and explicitly bound the validity domain in (P, Pdot, B) space.
mature_ideas.falsifier: A statistically significant population of young isolated pulsars with n > 3 or n < 1 that cannot be reproduced by any combination of dot{alpha} and eta within physically plausible ranges, or direct observation of B-field decay in non-magnetar pulsars on spin-down timescales.
mature_ideas.lineage: Derived from gap:sh4:missing_assumption:assumption and gap:sh2:mechanism_explanation_gap:candidate_mechanism, using survey evidence on inclination angle decay (W2590059791) and Crab pulsar wind braking (W2039864550).

mature_ideas.title: Ablation-Transition Boundary via Irradiation Flux Threshold
mature_ideas.hypothesis: The transition from stable recycling to companion ablation is governed by a critical irradiation flux threshold F_crit that depends on companion mass and orbital period, beyond which hydrodynamic escape dominates over Roche lobe overflow.
mature_ideas.central_hypothesis: The transition from stable recycling to companion ablation is governed by a critical irradiation flux threshold F_crit that depends on companion mass and orbital period, beyond which hydrodynamic escape dominates over Roche lobe overflow.
mature_ideas.mechanism: Define F_crit(M_c, P_orb) from energy balance between pulsar wind heating and companion gravitational binding energy; fit to black widow and redback populations to recover the threshold surface; validate against SAX J1808.4-3658 orbital period derivative.
mature_ideas.mechanism_or_relation: Define F_crit(M_c, P_orb) from energy balance between pulsar wind heating and companion gravitational binding energy; fit to black widow and redback populations to recover the threshold surface; validate against SAX J1808.4-3658 orbital period derivative.
mature_ideas.falsifier: Compare predicted ablation onset orbital periods against observed black widow/redback population; test whether systems near F_crit exhibit transitional X-ray/radio states.

mature_ideas.title: rotor dynamics and control theory
mature_ideas.hypothesis: The pulsar magnetic inclination angle alpha(t) is formally analogous to a rotor misalignment angle; the decay rate dot{alpha} acts as an anisotropic damping term that modifies the effective torque. This mapping justifies the functional form N(Omega) = -K Omega^3 [sin^2(alpha(t)) + eta(t)] and provides physical intuition for why n_eff deviates from 3 without requiring B-field decay.
mature_ideas.central_hypothesis: The pulsar magnetic inclination angle alpha(t) is formally analogous to a rotor misalignment angle; the decay rate dot{alpha} acts as an anisotropic damping term that modifies the effective torque. mature_ideas.mechanism: Time-varying misalignment angle in rotating machinery with anisotropic damping, where the effective braking torque depends on both the angle and its secular drift rate.
